newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil BNDES disbursements rise 19 pct in 12 mths.
newsitem.headline: Brazil BNDES disbursements rise 19 pct in 12 mths.

text.p: Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) has disbursed $10.56 billion worth in loans and investments over the last year, up 19 percent from $8.85 billion in the previous 12-month period.

BNDES President Luiz Carlos Mendonca de Barros said the bank's disbursements increased mainly in the North of Brazil where they jumped 112 percent to $311 million between July 1996 and June 1997 from $147 million in the previous 12-month period.

BNDES funding in the South increased 42 percent to $2.9 billion, 37 percent in the Center-East to $740 million, 36 percent in the Northeast to $1.37 billion and only three percent in the Southeast to $5.24 billion.

BNDES financing increased most in the infrastructure sector, up 57 percent at $3.79 billion from $2.41 billion previously, followed by the agricultural sector, up 32 percent at $920 million, and trade and services, up 11 percent at $1.22 billion.
Brazilian industry received the largest amount of BNDES funding in the last 12 months with $4.64 billion, followed by infrastructure, and trade and services.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
